items.recapEn: On Obon night in Shimada the Ōi river lay low and braided. Hana wrote that even if it rained they would cross by the long bridge, and that the more she walked the more she noticed. The inn's grandmother Okada-san lit a lantern for old travellers and gave Hana a cold towel. Far to the east, small, Fuji showed again.

items.recapEn: On the riverbank Hana asked whether they would cross even if it rained; Ken said even if. His noodle tally came out: thirty-one bowls. Tanaka-san appeared, announced five past four and forecast rain, so Ken concluded tomorrow would be fine. Hana, switching to polite forms, promised to meet him at the bridge; he will come by train.

items.recapEn: A postcard to her mother from Shimada on Obon night: lanterns at the doors, the famous river almost all sand, even if it rains they cross by the long bridge, and the more she walks the more she sees. Ken is fine and at thirty-one bowls; Fuji showed small and far. She apologises for the too-polite phone call.
